content:

በዚህ ክፍል፦ Scarcity, Choice, Opportunity Cost, Production Possibilities Frontier (PPF/PPC)፣ የPPF ስሌቶች፣ Economic Growth እና Basic Economic Questions (What, How, For Whom) የሚሉትን በፈተናዎች ላይ ሁልጊዜ የሚደጋገሙ ወሳኝ ፅንሰ-ሐሳቦች በጥልቀትና በፍፁም በማይሰለች አቀራረብ እንመለከታለን። አብራችሁኝ ሁኑ👇👇👇


1.4 Scarcity, Choice, Opportunity Cost and Production Possibilities Frontier (PPF)

Have you ever faced a problem of choice among different alternatives? If yes, what was your decision? What is scarcity, and do you think it is different from shortage? Why?

It is often said that the central purpose of economic activity is the production of goods and services to satisfy consumer's needs and wants—i.e., to meet people's need for consumption both as a means of survival and also to meet their ever-growing demand for an improved lifestyle or standard of living.

1. Scarcity

The fundamental economic problem that any human society faces is the problem of scarcity. Scarcity refers to the fact that all economic resources that a society needs to produce goods and services are finite or limited in supply. But their being limited should be expressed in relation to human wants. Thus, the term scarcity reflects the fundamental imbalance between our wants and the means available to satisfy those wants.

Classification of Resources:
Resources are categorized based on their availability into two major groups:
• Free Resources: A resource is said to be free if the amount available to a society is greater than the amount people desire at zero price (e.g., sunshine, atmospheric air, ocean water).
• Scarce (Economic) Resources: A resource is said to be scarce or an economic resource when the amount available to a society is less than what people want to have at zero price.

Examples of Scarce Resources:
• Human resources: Manual, intellectual, skilled, and specialized labor.
• Natural resources: Fertile land, minerals, clean water, forests, and wild animals.
• Capital resources: Machinery, intermediate goods, equipment, and infrastructure.
• Entrepreneurial resources: Innovation, organizational leadership, and risk-taking abilities.

Economic resources are systematically classified into four major factors of production:
1. Labor: Refers to the physical as well as mental efforts of human beings in the production and distribution of goods and services. The reward/return for labor is called wage.
2. Land: Refers to all natural resources or all the free gifts of nature usable in the production of goods and services. The reward for the services of land is known as rent.
3. Capital: Refers to all manufactured inputs that can be used to produce other goods and services (e.g., equipment, machinery, transport and communication facilities). The reward for capital is called interest.
4. Entrepreneurship: Refers to a special type of human talent that helps to organize and manage other factors of production to produce goods and services and takes the risk of making losses. The reward for entrepreneurship is called profit.

Entrepreneurs are individuals who:
• Organize factors of production to produce goods and services.
• Make basic business policy decisions.
• Introduce new inventions and technologies into business practice.
• Look for new business opportunities.
• Take risks of making losses.

👉 የእጥረትና የሀብት ክፍፍል (ከስር የተብራራ):
• የእጥረት (Scarcity) ፅንሰ-ሐሳብ፦ የሰው ልጅ ፍላጎት ወሰን የለውም፤ ነገር ግን ፍላጎቱን የሚያሟሉ ሀብቶች (Resources) ውስን ናቸው። ይህ በምኞታችንና ባለን ሀብት መካከል ያለው አለመጣጣን Scarcity (እጥረት) ይባላል።
• የሀብቶች አይነት፦ ሀብቶች በሁለት ይከፈላሉ፦
  1) Free Resources፦ ያለ ምንም ክፍያ በበቂ ሁኔታ የምናገኛቸው ናቸው (ለምሳሌ፡ የፀሐይ ብርሃን፣ አየር)።
  2) Economic Resources፦ በከንቱ የማናገኛቸውና ውስን የሆኑ ናቸው።
• አራቱ የምርት ሀብቶች (4 Factors of Production) እና ክፍያዎቻቸው፦
  1) Labor (ጉልበት)፦ የሰው ልጅ አካላዊና አእምሯዊ ጥረት ሲሆን ክፍያው Wage (ደሞዝ) ይባላል።
  2) Land (መሬት/ተፈጥሮ)፦ ማንኛውም የተፈጥሮ ስጦታ ሲሆን ክፍያው Rent (ኪራይ) ይባላል።
  3) Capital (ካፒታል)፦ ለሌሎች ምርቶች መስሪያ የሚያገለግሉ ማሽኖችና መሳሪያዎች ሲሆኑ ክፍያው Interest (ወለድ) ይባላል።
  4) Entrepreneurship (ስራ ፈጠራ)፦ ስጋት ወስዶ ሌሎች ሀብቶችን አደራጅቶ የሚመራ ችሎታ ሲሆን ክፍያው Profit (ትርፍ) ይባላል።

💡 Note: Scarcity does NOT mean Shortage!
Scarcity refers to a universal and everlasting situation where available resources are less than total human desires at zero price. Shortage is a specific, short-term market phenomenon where people are unable to get the amount they want at the prevailing market price (e.g., fuel shortage in a city).

👉 Scarcity vs Shortage ልዩነት (ከስር የተብራራ):
• Scarcity (እጥረት)፦ ዘላለማዊ፣ ሁልጊዜ ያለና አለም አቀፋዊ ችግር ነው። የሰው ልጅ ፍላጎት ከመሬት ሀብት ሁልጊዜ ስለሚበልጥ አይጠፋም።
• Shortage (አቅርቦት ማነስ)፦ ጊዜያዊ የሆነ የገበያ ችግር ነው። በዋጋ መዛባት ወይም በጊዜያዊ የምርት እጥረት ምክንያት የሚከሰትና አቅርቦት ሲጨምር የሚፈታ ነው (ለምሳሌ፡ በከተማ ውስጥ የነዳጅ አቅርቦት ለጥቂት ቀናት ማነስ)።


2. Choice

If resources are scarce, then output will be limited. If output is limited, then we cannot satisfy all of our wants. Thus, choice must be made. Due to the problem of scarcity, individuals, firms, and governments are forced to choose as to what output to produce, in what quantity, and what output not to produce.

In short: Scarcity implies Choice. Choice, in turn, implies Cost. That means whenever a choice is made, an alternative opportunity is sacrificed.

Scarcity → Limited Resources → Limited Output → Satisfy Limited Wants → Choice Involves Costs → Opportunity Cost

👉 የምርጫ አስፈላጊነት (ከስር የተብራራ):
ሀብት ውስን በመሆኑ ምክንያት ሁሉንም ፍላጎቶቻችንን ማሟላት አንችልም። ስለዚህ ግለሰቦች፣ ድርጅቶችና መንግስታት ከብዙ አማራጮች መካከል ምርጫ (Choice) ማድረግ አለባቸው። Scarcity ወደ Choice ይመራል፤ Choice ደግሞ Cost (መስዋዕትነት) ያስከትላል። አንድን ነገር ስንመርጥ ሌላውን የመተው ውሳኔ ለማድረግ እንገደዳለን።


3. Opportunity Cost

In a world of scarcity, a decision to have more of one thing, at the same time, means a decision to have less of another thing. The value of the next best alternative that must be sacrificed is, therefore, the opportunity cost of the decision.

Definition: Opportunity cost is the amount or value of the next best alternative that must be sacrificed (forgone) in order to obtain one more unit of a product.

Example: Suppose a country spends all of its limited resources on the production of cloth or computer. If a given amount of resources can produce either 1 meter of cloth or 20 units of computer, then the cost of 1 meter of cloth is the 20 units of computer that must be sacrificed in order to produce a meter of cloth.

When we say opportunity cost, we mean that:
• It is measured in real goods and services (or time), not merely in money costs.
• It should be in line with the principle of substitution.
In conclusion, when the opportunity cost of an activity increases, people substitute other activities in its place.

👉 የዕድል መስዋዕትነት - Opportunity Cost (ከስር የተብራራ):
• ትርጉም፦ አንድን ነገር ለማግኘት ስንል የምንተወው ሁለተኛው የተሻለው አማራጭ (Next Best Alternative) የዚያ ውሳኔ Opportunity Cost ይባላል።
• መለኪያ፦ የሚለካው በተተውት እቃዎች፣ አገልግሎቶች ወይም ሰዓት እንጂ በገንዘብ ብቻ አይደለም።
• ምሳሌ፦ ባለን ሀብት 1 ሜትር ጨርቅ ወይም 20 ኮምፒዩተር ማምረት ብንችል፣ 1 ሜትር ጨርቅ ለማምረት የምንተወው 20 ኮምፒዩተር የጨርቁ Opportunity Cost ነው።


4. The Production Possibilities Frontier or Curve (PPF/PPC)

The Production Possibilities Frontier (PPF) is a curve or graph that shows the various maximum possible combinations of two goods and services that a society can produce given its limited resources and current state of technology.

Assumptions to draw the PPF:
a. The quantity as well as quality of economic resources available for use during the year is fixed.
b. There are only two broad classes of output to be produced over the year (e.g., Food and Computers).
c. The economy is operating at full employment and is achieving full production (efficiency).
d. Technology does not change during the year.
e. Some inputs are better adapted to the production of one good than to the production of the other (resource specialization).

Graphical Illustration of PPF:

Food (Y)5004203201800A •B •C •D •E •Q • (Inefficient)R • (Unattainable)Computer (X)500100015002000
Figure 1.1: Production Possibilities Frontier (Concave Shape)

The PPF describes three important concepts:
i) Concept of Scarcity: Society cannot have unlimited output even if it employs all resources. This is represented by unattainable points outside the curve (e.g., Point R).
ii) Concept of Choice: Any movement along the curve indicates a change in choice among efficient alternatives.
iii) Concept of Opportunity Cost: Producing more of one good requires sacrificing some of another, reflected by the downward slope of the PPF.

👉 የPPF ፅንሰ-ሐሳብና የነጥቦች ማብራሪያ (ከስር የተብራራ):
• PPF ምንድን ነው?፦ ባለን ውስን ሀብትና ቴክኖሎጂ ማምረት የምንችለውን ከፍተኛው የሁለት ምርቶች ውህደት የሚያሳይ ግራፍ ነው።
• የነጥቦቹ ትርጉም፦
  1) በመስመሩ ላይ ያሉ ነጥቦች (A, B, C, D, E)፦ ሀብታችን በሙሉ አቅሙና በብቃት ስራ ላይ መዋሉን ያሳያሉ (Full Employment & Efficiency)።
  2) ከመስመሩ ውስጥ ያለ ነጥብ (Q)፦ የሀብት ብክነት ወይም ስራ አጥነት መኖሩን ያሳያል (Inefficient/Underemployment)።
  3) ከመስመሩ ውጪ ያለ ነጥብ (R)፦ አሁን ባለን ሀብትና ቴክኖሎጂ ልንደርስበት የማንችለው ግብ ነው (Unattainable)።

Mathematical Formula for Opportunity Cost on PPF:

Opportunity Cost of Good X = | ΔGood Y / ΔGood X | = | Amount of Alternative Sacrificed / Amount of Good Gained |


Numerical Example:
Question: Suppose an economy moves from production combination Alternative B (producing 420 Metric Tons of Food and 500 units of Computers) to Alternative C (producing 320 Metric Tons of Food and 1000 units of Computers). What is the opportunity cost of producing 1 additional unit of Computer?

Given Parameters:
• At Point B (Initial Position): Food = 420 metric tons, Computers = 500 units
• At Point C (New Position): Food = 320 metric tons, Computers = 1000 units

Step-by-Step Calculation:
• Change in Food Output (ΔGood Y) = 320 - 420 = -100 metric tons (Food Sacrificed)
• Change in Computer Output (ΔGood X) = 1000 - 500 = 500 units (Computers Gained)

OC of 1 Computer = | (320 - 420) / (1000 - 500) | = | -100 / 500 | = 0.2 metric tons of Food


Interpretation: To produce 1 additional unit of computer, the economy gives up 0.2 metric tons of food.

👉 የPPF ስሌት ማብራሪያ (ከስር የተብራራ):
ቀመሩ Opportunity Cost = | የተተወው እቃ መጠን (ΔY) ÷ የተገኘው እቃ መጠን (ΔX) | ነው።
ከነጥብ B ወደ C ስንሄድ የተተወው ምግብ = 420 - 320 = 100፤ የተገኘው ኮምፒዩተር = 1000 - 500 = 500።
ስለዚህ የ 1 ኮምፒዩተር OC = 100 / 500 = 0.2 የምግብ መጠን ይሆናል! ማለትም አንድ ተጨማሪ ኮምፒዩተር ለማምረት 0.2 ምግብ መስዋዕት እናደርጋለን።

The Law of Increasing Opportunity Cost:
As we produce more and more units of a product, the opportunity cost per unit of the additional output increases. This law makes the shape of the PPF concave to the origin (bowed outward). The reason why opportunity cost increases is that economic resources are not completely adaptable to alternative uses (specialization effect).

💡 Exam Hint: ፈተና ላይ 'Why is the PPF concave to the origin?' ተብሎ ከተጠየቀ መልሱ፦ 'Due to the Law of Increasing Opportunity Cost' ወይም 'Because resources are not perfectly adaptable to alternative uses' የሚለው ነው። መልሷን እንዳትረሱ!

👉 የህጉና የቅርፁ ማብራሪያ (ከስር የተብራራ):
አንድን እቃ እየጨመርን ባመርን ቁጥር ለሱ የምንከፍለው Opportunity Cost እየጨመረ ይሄዳል። ይህ Law of Increasing Opportunity Cost ይባላል። የPPF ግራፍ Concave (ወደ ውጭ ያበጠ/Bowed outward) የሆነበት ምክንያት ሀብቶች ለሁሉም ስራ እኩል ብቁ ስላልሆኑ (Resources are not perfectly adaptable) ነው!


5. Economic Growth and the PPF

Economic growth or an increase in the total output level occurs when one or both of the following conditions occur:
1. Increase in the quantity and/or quality of economic resources.
2. Advances in technology.

Representation on PPF:
• Symmetric (Outward) Shift: Economic growth is represented by an outward shift of the entire PPF curve if resources or technology improve for both goods.
• Asymmetric Shift: An economy can also grow because of an increase in productivity in only one sector. An improvement in technology applied to either food or computer is illustrated by a shift of the PPF along the Y-axis or X-axis only.

(B) Asymmetric Growth

👉 የኢኮኖሚ ዕድገትና የPPF ሽግግር (ከስር የተብራራ):
• የዕድገት መንስኤዎች፦ የሀብት መጠን/ጥራት መጨመር ወይም የቴክኖሎጂ ማደግ።
• የሽግግር አይነቶች፦
  1) Symmetric Shift (እኩል ሽግግር)፦ የሁለቱም ምርቶች ቴክኖሎጂ/ሀብት እኩል ሲያድግ ሙሉው የPPF መስመር ወደ ውጭ ይሸጋገራል።
  2) Asymmetric Shift (ያልተመጣጠነ ሽግግር)፦ የአንዱ ምርት ቴክኖሎጂ ብቻ ሲሻሻል (ለምሳሌ የኮምፒዩተር ብቻ) የPPF መስመር በዚያ ምርት አክሲስ በኩል ብቻ ወደ ውጭ ይለጠጣል።


1.5 Basic Economic Questions

Economic problems faced by an economic system due to scarcity of resources are known as basic economic problems. These problems are common to all economic systems. Therefore, any human society should answer the following three basic questions:

1. What to Produce? (Problem of Allocation of Resources)
Implies that every economy must decide which goods and in what quantities are to be produced. The economy must make choices such as consumption goods versus capital goods, civil goods versus military goods, and necessity goods versus luxury goods.

👉 1. ምን ይመረት? - What to Produce? (ከስር የተብራራ):
ይህ የሀብት ድልድል (Allocation of Resources) ጥያቄ ነው። ሀገር ያላትን ውስን ሀብት ተጠቅማ ምን አይነት እቃና አገልግሎት (ለምሳሌ፡ ምግብ ወይስ የጦር መሳሪያ?) በምን ያህል መጠን ማምረት እንዳለባት የምትወስነው ውሳኔ ነው።

2. How to Produce? (Problem of Choice of Technique)
Once an economy has reached a decision regarding the types and quantities of goods to be produced, it must decide how to produce them—choosing between alternative methods or techniques of production.

Techniques of production are classified into two groups:
• Labor-Intensive Technique: Involves the use of more labor relative to capital per unit of output.
• Capital-Intensive Technique: Involves the use of more capital relative to labor per unit of output.

👉 2. እንዴት ይመረት? - How to Produce? (ከስር የተብራራ):
ይህ የቴክኖሎጂ መረጣ (Choice of Technique) ጥያቄ ነው። ምርቱ በምን አይነት መንገድ ይመረት የሚለውን ይወስናል፦
• Labor-Intensive፦ ከማሽን ይልቅ የሰው ጉልበት አብዝቶ መጠቀም።
• Capital-Intensive፦ ከሰው ጉልበት ይልቅ ማሽኖችንና ቴክኖሎጂን አብዝቶ መጠቀም።

3. For Whom to Produce? (Problem of Distribution of National Product)
Relates to how a material product is to be distributed among the members of a society. The economy must decide whether to produce for the benefit of the few rich people or for the large number of poor people.

👉 3. ለማን ይመረት? - For Whom to Produce? (ከስር የተብራራ):
ይህ የምርት ክፍፍል (Distribution of National Product) ጥያቄ ነው። የተመረተው እቃና አገልግሎት ለህብረተሰቡ አባላት እንዴት መከፋፈል አለበት? (ለጥቂት ሀብታሞች ወይስ ለብዙሃኑ ድሆች?) የሚለውን ውሳኔ ይመለከታል።
